instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: M-002 through M-004 establish cleanup as an event-backed, DRY-sequenced subsystem with widget reuse and Interaction Mode copy separation. Adversarially, they do not enumerate the event schema, rollup invariants, or a complete copy matrix, so two conforming builders could emit incompatible events or materially different GUI explanations while passing the lineage-only acceptance criteria.
atoms.title: Cleanup event architecture is explicit but its payload and copy oracles are incomplete

atoms.statement: M-005 through M-010 form a coherent safety boundary: interview owns AGENTS generation, MiscPlan owns centralized cleanup policy, assistant worktrees persist by default, cleanup targets only the run's selected workspace, modes default conservatively, and duplicated allowlists or git-clean logic are forbidden. The adversarial destructive-action, cross-lane, secret-path, and ownership-confusion cases are directly constrained rather than silently delegated.
atoms.title: Cleanup protection, isolation, and DRY ownership form a strong non-gap

atoms.statement: M-011 through M-016 correctly centralize secret-safe git handling, before/after boundaries, wrapper adoption, and agent-output clearing. The exact contract is incomplete for process-tree termination, escalation timeout, cleanup error precedence, and the observable state of best-effort prepare skips; exhaustive caller adoption is stated but no machine-checkable caller inventory/oracle is supplied.
atoms.title: Runner cleanup lacks complete termination, skip, and caller-adoption oracles

atoms.statement: M-017 through M-022 establish one config projection, manual-clean safety, documentation, partitioned GUI state, and out-of-hot-path pruning. The phrase 'when feasible' leaves current/in-progress evidence protection non-normative; retain-last-runs ordering, active-run detection, prune concurrency/atomicity, partial deletion recovery, and the objective threshold for moving controls to a ninth tab remain unspecified.
atoms.title: Evidence pruning races and cleanup-control placement remain underspecified

atoms.statement: M-023 and M-024 precisely separate internal cleanup responsibility from provider extensions and provide exact Cursor copy oracles. M-025 through M-028 define a shared shortcut registry, visible active bindings, conflict/config recovery, and import/export. Adversarially, the canonical UI location is intentionally unchosen, 'all focusable text areas' lacks a closed registry, replace/merge transaction boundaries are not explicit, and reject-versus-steal, unknown-action, unknown-version, and overrides-versus-full-map choices remain builder discretion.
atoms.title: Shortcut contracts are rich but location, scope, and atomic import behavior remain open

atoms.statement: M-029 through M-034 define package validation, permission-gated loading, GUI mutations, PM-native readiness, and per-target projection drift boundaries. The exact cross-layer precedence among Persona defaults, explicit skill rules, wildcard rules, and runtime asks is spread across units rather than expressed as one total decision table; edit/import/remove/config-write operations also lack a complete transaction and concurrent-disk-change state machine, while final surface placement is delegated to owner docs.
atoms.title: Skills core needs a total permission decision table and transactional mutation model

atoms.statement: M-035 through M-040 preserve important decisions for deduplication, no-overwrite creation, ask timing, pattern precedence, retryable save failure, in-memory controls, on-demand preview, and mtime degradation. Adversarially, the units do not define snapshot/version binding between discovery, bulk match confirmation, persist retry, preview load, and metadata display, and they provide no explicit scale bounds or accessible/localized behavior for large tables and error states.
atoms.title: Advanced Skills flows need snapshot consistency, scale, and retry-state oracles

atoms.statement: The baseline names a calendar date and live web/API access but no immutable commit, tag digest, archive hash, or per-artifact revision binding.
atoms.title: The deterministic baseline is not immutably pinned

atoms.statement: The command baseline exposes shell execution and file/agent resolution but this source does not specify sanitization, provenance, sandbox, path traversal, symlink, or approval boundaries for those untrusted inputs.
atoms.title: Command template execution lacks an explicit trust boundary

atoms.statement: Approval blocking and reject-all behavior are described, but the negative-space lifecycle for abandoned, duplicated, disconnected, or restored requests is absent.
atoms.title: Approval requests have no complete recovery state machine

atoms.statement: The second prologue continuation explicitly maps extracted topics to PM owners and records PM-specific divergences across run modes, permissions, commands, formatters, skills, plugins, and models.
atoms.title: Owner routing and PM delta hooks are explicit

atoms.statement: The baseline describes remote downloads and package installation/import but provides no complete trust, integrity, authority, privacy, or rollback contract for extension supply chains.
atoms.title: Remote skills and plugins lack supply-chain controls

atoms.statement: Formatter discovery and direct process invocation are specified, but execution, concurrency, partial-failure, rollback, and observability semantics are not.
atoms.title: Formatter subprocess behavior is operationally under-specified

atoms.statement: ODE-001 explicitly retires source-preserving ownership, delegates coverage to fine-grained units or structural dispositions, and forbids executable task creation.
atoms.title: ODE-001 has a clear terminal compatibility disposition

atoms.statement: ODE-002 through ODE-004 atomize document governance, the dated upstream baseline, and the broad extraction goal without claiming runtime ownership.
atoms.title: Governance, baseline, and extraction scope are separately atomized

atoms.statement: ODE-005 names an assistance capability floor and /no-secrets boundary but does not bind each capability to allowed actions, resource scopes, prompt/approval requirements, or denial oracles.
atoms.title: The preserved assistance floor lacks an exact authority matrix

atoms.statement: ODE-006 through ODE-008 preserve transfer tokens, route runtime and usage references to owning documents, and classify command-shaped coverage hazards as evidence only.
atoms.title: Token fidelity and evidence-only routing are guarded

atoms.statement: ODE-009 through ODE-012 preserve broad historical, orchestration, legacy-tier, routing, and model-cohort labels but do not define a closed-loop reconciliation protocol for those labels.
atoms.title: Audit-lineage labels lack a terminal reconciliation oracle

atoms.statement: ODE-013 through ODE-016 establish deterministic inputs, ordered extraction and normalization, a six-field downstream record, and acceptance rules for single-owner mapping and lock preservation.
atoms.title: Extraction inputs, procedure, outputs, and acceptance are atomized

atoms.statement: ODE-017 and ODE-018 preserve the plan-mode restrictions, exit mechanism, synthetic agent switch, AgentPart bypass, and build reminder as upstream baseline behavior.
atoms.title: Plan-to-build switching behavior is explicitly preserved

atoms.statement: ODE-019 and ODE-020 enumerate approval outcomes and agent fields but omit lifecycle, GUI truth, validation, and authority constraints needed for a production contract.
atoms.title: Approval and agent metadata remain structurally under-constrained

atoms.statement: ODE-021 and ODE-022 capture built-in/user-defined agent controls and the task-based subagent execution sequence, including running state, hooks, and merged permissions.
atoms.title: Agent configuration and subagent invocation are represented

atoms.statement: ODE-023 through ODE-025 describe read-only exploration, transformable prompt assembly, and destructive compaction without a complete capability-level mutation guard, plugin trust order, or recoverable context-integrity contract.
atoms.title: Read-only execution and prompt/compaction integrity are not enforced end to end

atoms.statement: ODE-026 through ODE-028 define rule shape, last-match precedence, and wildcard syntax but not normalization, provenance, race isolation, traversal/symlink handling, or cross-platform parity oracles.
atoms.title: Permission matching is syntactically clear but security semantics are incomplete

atoms.statement: ODE-029 through ODE-031 define guard defaults, once/always/reject behavior, and .env patterns, but omit request identity and ordering, stale/offline GUI handling, and a broader secret-classification lifecycle.
atoms.title: Permission UI lifecycle and secret-file protection remain incomplete

atoms.statement: ODE-032 through ODE-035 preserve discovery, metadata, template execution, delegation, model override, and name-collision behavior without a complete trust and precedence contract.
atoms.title: Command discovery and override create an unbounded execution seam

atoms.statement: ODE-036 defines automatic sequential formatting after edit events but not deduplication, reentrancy, ordering across files, cancellation, failure isolation, rollback, or observability.
atoms.title: Automatic formatter triggering lacks concurrency and recovery semantics

cross_document_questions: Which owning contract pins every OpenCode extraction run to an immutable upstream revision and exact artifact hashes?

Which Permissions, Commands, Skills, Plugins, and Tools owner sections define provenance, sandboxing, override authority, path canonicalization, and denial oracles for shell, file, remote, and extension inputs?

Which HITL and GUI owner defines request identity, timeout, cancellation, reconnect, restart recovery, concurrent reply ordering, accessible labels, localization, and stale-state presentation for approvals?
Which Formatter and event owner defines debounce, reentrancy, per-file serialization, timeout, exit handling, partial-write rollback, retry, diagnostics, and loop prevention?
Which migration or coverage owner adjudicates and terminally retires the historical routing, tier-era, ghost, cohort, and owner-of-owners lineage labels?
research_seed_queries: Immutable source pinning and artifact attestation patterns for upstream reference extraction
Secure command template expansion for shell execution and file inclusion
Plugin and remote skill supply-chain signing sandboxing revocation and cache integrity
Concurrent approval workflow idempotency timeout reconnect and crash recovery state machines
Reentrant file formatter event loops transactional writes rollback and failure isolation
Cross-platform wildcard path canonicalization symlink traversal and permission matching parity
